title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：protest　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 protest 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1975 the clerk ① held the protest that no applicant in the office would have measured, and he said the holding was the whole of the month. The ② protest, meaning the objection itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book; a protest, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ protest in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ protest at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A protest, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the clerk said the measuring is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the protest was the whole of the matter, meaning the courage and not the objection. The ⑥ protest, meaning the courage and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; protest, he said, is either something you hold or the only word that means both an objection and a courage. He said the courage is the part they remember.

By 1980 the ⑦ protest had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ protest of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of measuring; protest, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ protest I remember is the objection measured in the file, which closed in 1982 and is still measured as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ protest, my mother said in 1984, is the only objection that improves by being measured; every protest, she said, is a courage that has agreed to look like an objection. She said the courage was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 抗议；反对（指办事处里每一场旁边的那一场）
B. n. 抗议；反对（指那场抗议本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold the protest 举行这一场抗议
D. n. 抗议；反对（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 抗议之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的抗议之事）
F. n. 抗议；反对（指卷宗里写到、被测量的那一场）
G. n. 抗议、血气（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 血气（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: held the protest that no applicant in the office would have measured
The protest, meaning the objection itself and not the stamp
the protest at the far counter
the protest was the whole of the matter
the protest had become a line in a file
The protest of the whole thing
A protest, my mother said in 1984

answers.why: hold the protest 意为“举行这一场抗议”，1975 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯测量的一场抗议做了一遍。
protest 意为“抗议；反对”，指那场抗议本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。
protest 意为“抗议；反对”，指办事处里每一场旁边的那一场，每一场旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
protest 意为“抗议；反对”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
protest 意为“抗议、血气”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这场血气就是那件事的全部。
protest 意为“血气”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那场抗议，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
protest 意为“抗议；反对”，指卷宗里写到、被测量的那一场，到 1980 年这一场成了卷宗里的一行。
protest 意为“抗议之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的抗议之事是一处办事处和三个月份的测量。
protest 意为“抗议；反对”，我记得的是卷宗里测量过的那一场，1982 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一场。
protest 为抽象总称，母亲 1984 年说，抗议是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的抗议。
